text.content:
Tucked into a switchback in the passage is a shallow niche, clearly shaped by hand rather than chance. A crude effigy - fleece stretched over sticks, capped with a real, sun-bleached skull - watches the corridor with obvious reverence built around it: melted candle stubs, a scattering of coins, a single chewed boot left as an offering.

GM Notes

Breather: No threat here. This is pure color, and it's the clearest evidence yet that the goblins' llama-worship predates Corvin - he didn't invent this, he just inherited a warren that was already primed for it.

Subquest - The Shrine: Leaving an offering (anything small) is noted approvingly by any goblin who happens to see it - purely a reputation gesture, worth a friendlier reception elsewhere on the floor if you want to track that. Desecrating it is noted just as clearly, the other direction.
